records.name: We Love Philly
records.summary: A nonprofit that works to transform education for Philadelphia students through paid digital marketing and cybersecurity pre-apprenticeships. Adults can volunteer, join a committee, or mentor.
records.what_you_do: Students gain hands-on work experience in the classroom and earn wages through the pre-apprenticeships. Adults can start on the Get Involved page by taking the volunteer survey, booking a tour, or signing up through the Become a Mentor page.

cost.text: The pages we read do not say whether volunteering or mentoring costs anything. Donations are accepted, and apprentices earn wages.

first_step.how: Take the volunteer survey on the Get Involved page, or book a tour through the Volunteer or Schedule a Tour page. Mentors can start from the Become a Mentor page.
first_step.basis: The way in is a survey or a tour booking, and the pages we read do not say what a volunteer does or what a first visit is like.

records.notes: Own site is thin. The Volunteer or Schedule a Tour, Become a Mentor and Get Involved pages show links and a survey but no detail on volunteer tasks, hours, fees or a first visit, so those fields keep their tier 1 values and what_to_expect is left out. The events page lists a workshop on Sept 30, 2026 (6 to 8 pm, 3675 Market Street) and virtual volunteer mock interviews for students on Oct 5 to 9, 2026; both are one-time items and are kept out of schedule. The office address and info@ email come from the contact page. The IRS address is kept. No FAQ page found.

records.name: ArtistYear
records.summary: A national AmeriCorps program that places full time teaching artists in K to 12 schools and community settings, including in Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Apply to serve as a full time ArtistYear Fellow teaching in schools or communities for 6 or 10 months. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the slots are filled.

schedule.text: Full time service: 10 months from a September start, or 6 months from a January start

cost.text: Fellows get a monthly living stipend and, if they need one, a health insurance stipend. The amounts are not stated on the pages we read. Fellows also earn an education award after finishing the service year.

first_step.how: Check the eligibility rules on the Apply Now page, then submit the online application for the 2026 to 2027 program year. Most regions are full, and the page names open spots only in Piedmont, SC and the Roaring Fork Valley, CO, so check that page for current openings before you apply.
first_step.basis: The way in is a formal application that asks for an arts degree or comparable experience, U.S. citizenship or legal residency, and passing background checks.
first_step.what_to_expect: A fellow works full time as a teaching artist in a school, teaching standards-based arts lessons, leading at least one community arts project a year, and attending required training. Service runs 10 months from a September start or 6 months from a January start, with a monthly stipend.

records.notes: The Apply Now page names the 2026 to 2027 program year without a month, so last_sign_of_life is left empty and status stays probably_active. The stipend amount, Philadelphia start dates and any deadline are not stated on the pages read. The contact page lists a Gladwyne, PA mailing address outside the city, which was not added, and a Philadelphia legal address (4431 Main Street, 19127), which is already in the record. Its only email on the page is for school partnerships, so it is not listed as an applicant contact. The pages say fellows must pass background checks and clearances for working with youth but do not name the Act 153 clearance, so act153_clearances is left out. Requirements for court orders and service hours letters are not stated.

records.name: Balanced Veterans Network
records.summary: A veteran-led community for veterans and their families, with peer support, education and wellness resources on topics such as the transition out of military service and suicide prevention.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the free online community through the website or the app. Members use a private platform for live and recorded education sessions, peer discussion spaces, and wellness resources. Its programs cover movement, mental wellness, and education on cannabis and psychedelic-assisted approaches, and its events page lists runs, retreats, and social gatherings.

schedule.text: Lists its runs, retreats, and social gatherings on its events page as they are scheduled.

cost.text: Membership is free, and donations are optional and tax-deductible. Most listed events are marked free; the Veterans Day event does not state a cost.

first_step.how: Click Join Today on the website, or download the group's app, and set up a free membership. The sign-up form asks for your name and email, and whether you are a veteran, an active duty member, or a civilian supporter.
first_step.basis: Membership is free and open to veterans, active duty members, and their families or supporters, with a clear online sign-up, though the site does not say what a typical event or online session feels like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Joining is online: once you sign up, the members' platform offers live and recorded education sessions, peer discussion spaces, and wellness resources. Some areas are reserved for veterans, and family members and supporters have their own spaces. The site does not say how long sessions last or who leads them.
first_visit_tips: Event listings do not say where events are held, so check the details before you travel to one.

records.notes: The events page lists 10 dated events for October and November 2026, including a Veterans Day event on Nov 1, two 5K runs, a gravel bike race and several retreats. None gives a place and most give no sign-up step, so they stay out of schedule. Sign-up is self-reported: the form asks for veteran, active duty or civilian status but does not check it. Tier 1 listed the same IRS address twice; this record keeps one copy. The site does not name who runs the group or where it is based. Its advocacy programs on cannabis and psychedelic-assisted approaches are mentioned in what_you_do so first timers are not surprised.

records.name: Brenda's Cat Rescue
records.summary: An all-volunteer rescue for stray and abandoned cats. Cats live in foster homes until they are adopted, and the rescue also traps, neuters and returns feral cats from colonies.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat, adopt from the adoptable list, or help by socializing shy cats, driving cats to vet visits, or working at adoption events. Donations go through PayPal or Venmo, and the site also lists a barn cat program.

cost.text: The pages we read list no fee to volunteer. Foster homes pay for food, litter, and daily care, and the rescue covers vet costs for problems. Adoption fees are $150 for one adult cat, $225 for two adult cats, $175 for one kitten, and $275 for a pair of kittens, and they are not refundable.

first_step.how: Fill out the online foster application linked from the Foster page, or the online adoption application if you want to adopt. To ask about volunteering, use the contact form or email brendasrescues@gmail.com.
first_step.basis: Fostering and adopting both need a written application, and meeting cats happens only after approval; the volunteer roles are listed, but the way to start them is a contact form or email.
first_step.what_to_expect: After an adoption application is approved, the rescue arranges a meet and greet with the cat at the foster home. A foster keeps a cat for several weeks to several months, provides food, litter and daily care, and has vet costs covered for any problems.
first_visit_tips: Foster applicants must be at least 25 to be the main caretaker.
Adopters must be at least 21 and employed, self-employed or retired, and need a veterinarian reference and three personal references; incomplete applications are not processed.
Adoption preference goes to people living within one hour of Philadelphia.

records.notes: The site shows no dated items, so status stays probably_active with no last_sign_of_life. Fees come from the adoption page. The foster page does not say who handles pickup or drop-off, and no phone number is published. Tier 1 listed the same IRS address twice; this record keeps one copy. The contact page gives a mailing address of Suite 45 PMB 90, 701 Cathedral Road, which is the same suite Echo Collective uses in tier 1; donations by check go there. The rescue says it does not take surrenders of cats that people still own and points those owners to its Resources page. The barn cat program was named in navigation only and was not read.

records.name: East Falls Historical Society
records.summary: A society that records and shares the history of the East Falls neighborhood in Philadelphia through lectures, walking tours, oral histories, and an online archive. Its talks and tours are announced on the site.
records.what_you_do: Attend a talk, a Zoom lecture, or a walking tour, or explore the archive, photos, and oral histories online. Members can also volunteer for committees by emailing the society.

schedule.text: Holds Zoom lectures, in person talks, and walking tours through the year, including an annual winter Zoom program and an annual meeting. Each one is announced on the events page.

locations.label: Falls of Schuylkill Library meeting room

cost.text: Many talks are free. Walking tours have usually cost $15, or $10 for members, paid at the start. Membership can be joined online or by mailed form; the dues amounts were not shown on the page we read.

first_step.how: Pick a talk from the events page and use its Zoom link, or go to an in person talk at the Falls of Schuylkill Library meeting room. For the October 31, 2026 walking tour, email eastfallshistory@gmail.com, since the page gives no meeting place or sign-up steps.
first_step.basis: Talks and tours are open to the public with dates on the events page and a way to join by email or mail, though the site does not say it welcomes newcomers; some past tours needed booking ahead.
first_step.what_to_expect: Talks are given by a speaker, either on Zoom or at the library meeting room, and many are free. Walking tours run about an hour and a half to two hours in the morning, and members present their research on the places you visit.
first_visit_tips: Bring cash for a walking tour, since past tours were paid in cash at the start.
Email the society before the October 31, 2026 tour to learn the meeting place and time.

records.notes: Upcoming on the events page: a Zoom lecture on Sept 23, 2026 at 7 pm, and a walking tour on Oct 31, 2026 (morning, no exact time, details still to come). The about page gives 3501 Midvale Avenue as the society's mailing address, which is the Falls of Schuylkill Library. Tier 1's IRS address is an apartment (Apt D) and is kept in the record for owner review. Recent tours cost $10 to $15. The 2024 and 2025 events were used only to judge format and cost, not listed. Partners named on the site but not checked: NewCourtland, which hosts the Grace Kelly Gallery at 3232 Henry Ave, and the Preservation Alliance, named for a past lecture series. Neither has a URL on the pages read, so neither is in leads_only.

records.name: Echo Collective
records.summary: A collective that pairs political education with organizing, helping people make sense of the world and work toward change together.
records.what_you_do: Runs political education workshops and trainings, often built with partner organizations and groups, using games, storytelling, and small group work. It also offers facilitation help to groups that want to work in a more shared way. Its listed trainings give no dates, audience, or cost on the pages we read, so email to ask about the next one.

first_step.how: Email echocollective@proton.me and ask how to join the next workshop or training. The agenda page showed no dated sessions when we checked.
first_step.basis: The only public way in is an email, and the offers listed are mostly trainings and programs built with organizations and groups, with no open sessions named.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site describes its sessions as hands on and participatory, with people learning through games, storytelling, small group work, and shared reflection. The listed trainings run one week or three days on topics such as ecological breakdown and utopian thinking, but the pages do not say who can attend or what a first session is like.

records.notes: The our-work page lists three trainings: a one-week training on utopian perspectives, a one-week training on the roots of ecological breakdown, and a three-day unlearning workshop on the split between humans and non-humans. No dates, audience or cost are given for any of them. The agenda page showed no dated sessions. A summary of that page also said its archive holds three 2026 events without listing them; this could not be confirmed, so it is not used. The site does not say whether the work is nonpartisan. It names no party, candidate or ballot campaign, so the verdict stays publish and partisan is carried over as false from tier 1; the owner may want to confirm. The Collaborations page listing partner groups was not read. The mailing suite here (Suite 45 at 701 Cathedral Road) is the same suite Brenda's Cat Rescue uses for its mail.

notes: Batch of 7 groups: 6 records written, Manayunk Neighborhood Council not deepened (see blocked). Searches used 1 of 1 (hard cap). Fetches used 34 of the 60 allowed; no group went past 6. Manayunk: the one web search returned a summary, which I did not verify on the group's own site because that site refuses access. The summary says general meetings are on the first Wednesday of each month at 7 pm on Zoom, open to the public, with a next session listed for Nov 4, 2026. An older listing gave 7:30 pm at the Manayunk Development Corporation office at 4312 Main Street. Treat both as unverified until someone can read the group's own pages from another route, and do not publish them as fact. Cross-group: Brenda's Cat Rescue and Echo Collective both use Suite 45 at 701 Cathedral Road for mail, and the owner may want to know that two groups share one mailing suite. No group in this batch was found to be partisan, closed or outside Philadelphia.
